Okay, I've just traced all the places in the codebase that reference `config.max_seq_len`. The grep output shows five hits:

- The default value in `src/mythosmini/config.py` (line 64) – currently set to 512.
- The rope cache builder in `src/mythosmini/model/transformer.py` – uses `config.max_seq_len` to pre‑compute positional embeddings.
- The scorer in `src/mythosmini/benchmarks/scorer.py` – pulls `model.config.max_seq_len` into a local `max_len`.
- The runner in `src/mythosmini/benchmarks/runner.py` – also uses `model.config.max_seq_len` for the sequence length during evaluation.
- The wikitext benchmark in `src/mythosmini/benchmarks/wikitext.py` – presumably does the same.

I already opened `scorer.py` and saw that it simply reads `model.config.max_seq_len` into `max_len`. That suggests the benchmark code will also be pulling the same value. Since my next goal is to change the model's `max_seq_len` from its default 512 up to 1 M (as part of the plan to test a very long context), I need to verify that none of the benchmark utilities assume a small fixed length or otherwise hard‑code a limit. The scorer and runner are straightforward; they just use whatever the model reports. The only remaining unknown is the wikitext benchmark implementation – it could be slicing inputs, padding, or otherwise imposing a maximum length that would break if I simply set `max_seq_len` to 1 000 000.

Therefore, the logical next step is to inspect the contents of `src/mythosmini/benchmarks/wikitext.py`. Reading that file will let me see exactly how it constructs its evaluation dataset, whether it respects `model.config.max_seq_len`, and whether any changes will be required before I bump the sequence length. No other files seem relevant at this point; the other hits have already been examined or are trivial. So I’ll issue a read request for the wikitext benchmark module.
